text:
Sam: Quick follow-up from the all-hands Q&A. Sales asked we capture 1-2 bullets on why we won or lost recent deals and a single ask for leadership. Keep items short so we can triage.

Diego: Win: demos showed predictable p99 latency which resonated with a payments customer. Loss: competitor had a built-in signal routing plugin we don't support. Ask: a short decision doc for whether to prioritize signal-routing.

Avery: Lost a mid-market account because the Private setup felt heavy to their infra team. Ask: a one-page Private quickstart + an automated installer script.

Priya: Win theme: KV cache + batching cut token spend in demos, customers reacted positively to the numbers. Ask: produce a copy-paste benchmark snippet SEs can use.

Lina: CS notes: Console observability helped close deals; gaps: managed KMS/HSM integration is blocking a few enterprise buyers. Ask: target ETA for managed KMS.

Jordan: SE perspective: customers get confused by model variants and fallback behavior during demos. Ask: a one-page "which model to pick" guide with three buckets: latency, cost, quality.

Mali: Anecdote: a health tech customer picked us after an offline eval where caching reduced costs ~30%. They mentioned docs clarity sealed the decision. Ask: prioritize updating caching docs and examples.

Diego: Also saw procurement friction on reserved capacity contracts (billing cadence). Ask: sales + legal to draft a mid-market-friendly template.

Sam: Thanks. I'll convert these into a triage board tomorrow. Confirm with +1 or add one short item.

Avery: +1. Add: Console onboarding checklist for Private showing minimal steps and expected time.

Priya: +1. I'll draft the benchmark snippet and share later this week.

Lina: +1. I'll coordinate with Security and post a KMS ETA in #eng-security by EOD Friday.

Jordan: +1. Will draft the 3-bucket model guide and post to #eng-ml for review.

ops-bot: Reminder: all-hands follow-up survey will be sent out shortly.

Sam: Great thread. If anyone has short customer quotes (one line) add them here so we can cite in PRDs.
